review_type: Independent provider/source design review; no approval of reviewer-authored tests

frozen_details.v2_aad: literal bytes console.mail.credential\0\x02, then one purpose byte 1(payload) or 2(DEK wrap), then unchanged Aad.encode()
frozen_details.buffers: Zeroizing arrays and Vec own secret material before fallible operations; allocate checked payload+tag capacity before copying plaintext/DEK; avoid sensitive reallocation

checks: RandomizedNonceKey selects AES_256_GCM_RANDNONCE; pinned aws-lc-sys generates a fresh12byte IV internally with RAND_bytes on every seal and rejects external sealing IVs. Rust facade separates generated nonce from16byte tag; open recombines them only internally. Persisted12byte nonce and ciphertext+16tag are therefore correct; no manually managed counters or TLS-specific nonce mode are introduced.

RandomizedNonceKey open uses caller-provided retained nonce and performs authenticated gather through same AES primitive. Its checked_sub rejects too-short tags. Application helper must still enforce key32/nonce12 and map errors without plaintext; provider authentication failure may leave the in-place output touched, so Zeroizing must be installed before open, not after.

Exact new tuple nonce12/dek_nonce12/wrap49/marker02 is disjoint from legacy24/24/48. Marker is accepted only with full new tuple; legacy first wrapped byte is ciphertext and must never be treated as a marker. No fallback after AEAD failure. New domain+purpose binding and exact retained legacy AAD avoid ambiguous algorithm or field interpretation.

Actual PgMailStore persists separate SMTP/IMAP ciphertext/nonce/wrap groups and only one key_version; SMTP-only update writes that version, IMAP-only does not. Keeping KEK version1 and selecting format per field preserves mixed old/new secrets. BYTEA has no fixed nonce length and no schema mutation is required.

Zeroizing<Vec> wipes initialized data and spare capacity at drop, but cannot wipe old reallocations. Proposed capacity-before-sensitive-copy rule addresses this limitation. Generate DEK inside guarded32byte buffer; decrypt into guarded buffer; validate exact unwrapped32byte length before borrowing as key; transfer successful plaintext allocation into SecretBox only after both authenticated opens complete. Retained legacy decryption needs the same guards and should borrow Key::from_slice rather than create an unguarded owned key copy.

Provider-owned AES expanded contexts are LcPtr<EVP_AEAD_CTX>; drop invokes EVP_AEAD_CTX_free then OPENSSL_free, whose inspected implementation cleanses allocation. Pinned legacy ChaChaPoly1305 drop zeroizes its key. These provider memory and compiler/runtime contracts remain trusted assumptions; source review is not heap-remanence proof.

Rollback plan accurately excludes XChaCha-only readers after any AES write. Read compatibility must cover every app/send/sync worker and designated rollback binary before new writes begin; drain old consumers before activation. No historical reseal, key rotation, live deployment or credential access is implied.

Randomized96bit wrap nonce budget is aggregate per KEK across all processes/replicas and remains bounded at2^32 lifetime wrapping calls. Per-operation provider construction does not track that global budget. Documented budget and unresolved rotation/enforcement require operational qualification before exposure; this design does not claim them implemented.
implementation_obligations: Follow frozen exact tuple/AAD dispatch with no permissive parser or fallback.
Use checked capacity arithmetic and guard sensitive buffers before any failing operation, including legacy opens; avoid unguarded key copies.
Keep both legacy and AES readers, unchanged KEK version/env/AAD codec, historical bytes, migrations and current app owner port.
Obtain separate implementation, independent test, native runtime and real store preservation evidence.
limits: Reviewer performed source reads/hash checks and private receipt only; no builds/tests/SQL/network/repository edits.
This approves the concrete design, not its implementation, operational nonce-budget enforcement, FIPS certification, production rollout or reviewer-authored test packet.
